# React Native Sync Provider — Full API Reference

> React Native Nitro Module for offline-first HTTP sync. Requests are persisted natively (Core Data on iOS, Room on Android), retried with a persisted backoff, and flushed from JS or in OS-scheduled background windows (BGTaskScheduler, WorkManager).
> npm: @gabriel-sisjr/react-native-sync-provider
> Documentation: https://gabriel-sisjr.github.io/react-native-sync-provider/

## Installation

```bash
yarn add @gabriel-sisjr/react-native-sync-provider react-native-nitro-modules
# or
npm install @gabriel-sisjr/react-native-sync-provider react-native-nitro-modules
```

Requirements:
- React Native >= 0.74.0 with the New Architecture (Fabric + concurrent root) enabled.
- React >= 18.2.0.
- react-native-nitro-modules ^0.35.6.
- Android: minSdk 24, targetSdk 36, Kotlin 2.0+.
- iOS: 15+.

### iOS setup

1. Enable Background Modes `fetch` and `processing`.
2. Declare both fixed identifiers in Info.plist:

```xml
<key>BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers</key>
<array>
  <string>com.gabriel-sisjr.syncprovider.background</string>
  <string>com.gabriel-sisjr.syncprovider.processing</string>
</array>
```

3. Forward background URLSession events from a Swift AppDelegate:

```swift
import SyncProvider

func application(
  _ application: UIApplication,
  handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession identifier: String,
  completionHandler: @escaping () -> Void
) {
  HybridSyncProvider.handleBackgroundURLSessionEvents(
    identifier: identifier,
    completionHandler: completionHandler
  )
}
```

4. Run `cd ios && bundle exec pod install`.

The library registers its BGTask handlers at process start through +load. Do not call `BGTaskScheduler.shared.register` for its identifiers: iOS traps on a second registration.

### Android setup

Nothing to add. The manifest merger brings in INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED and BootCompletedReceiver.

## How dispatch works

- `enqueue` stores an item. It does not dispatch it, under any strategy.
- A flush dispatches. It comes from `useAutoSync`, `flush()`, `drainUntilEmpty()`, the retry timer, or an OS background window.
- A cycle takes one batch of eligible items, up to `batchSize`, ordered by priority and then age, and makes at most one attempt per item. Android sends a batch concurrently, iOS one item at a time.
- An item is eligible when it is PENDING and `nextRetryAt <= now`.
- On a retriable failure with attempts left, the item goes back to PENDING with `nextRetryAt` measured from the end of the attempt.
- A permanent failure leaves the item as a FAILED row. It is not returned by `getPendingItems()`, and nothing retries it.
- `AUTOMATIC` means the engine retries on its own: an in-process timer flushes when the soonest cooldown ends. It does not flush on enqueue or on reconnect.
- The timer never flushes offline. It remembers the wake and flushes when connectivity returns.
- Delivery is at least once.

## Quick Start

```typescript
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import {
  SyncProvider,
  useAutoSync,
  useSyncQueue,
  useSyncStatus,
  type SyncOptions,
} from '@gabriel-sisjr/react-native-sync-provider';

function Outbox() {
  useAutoSync({ enabled: true, flushOnAppForeground: true });
  const { items, enqueue } = useSyncQueue();
  const { lastResult, isSyncing } = useSyncStatus();

  return (
    <View>
      <Text>Pending: {items.length}</Text>
      <Text>Last flush ok: {lastResult?.successCount ?? 0}</Text>
      <Text>Syncing: {String(isSyncing)}</Text>
      <Button
        title="Send event"
        onPress={() =>
          enqueue({
            method: 'POST',
            url: 'https://api.example.com/events',
            contentType: 'application/json',
            body: JSON.stringify({ kind: 'login' }),
          })
        }
      />
    </View>
  );
}

export default function App({ token }: { token: string }) {
  const options = useMemo<SyncOptions>(
    () => ({
      strategy: 'AUTOMATIC',
      retryPolicy: {
        maxAttempts: 5,
        backoff: 'EXPONENTIAL',
        baseDelayMs: 1_000,
        maxDelayMs: 60_000,
        jitter: true,
        retryOnStatusCodes: [408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504],
      },
      defaultHeaders: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
    }),
    [token]
  );

  return (
    <SyncProvider options={options}>
      <Outbox />
    </SyncProvider>
  );
}
```

## Queue Functions

```typescript
function enqueue(item: SyncItemInput): Promise<string>;
function enqueueBatch(items: SyncItemInput[]): Promise<string[]>;
function removeItem(id: string): Promise<boolean>;
function clearQueue(): Promise<void>;
function getQueueSize(): Promise<number>;
function getPendingItems(): Promise<SyncItem[]>;
```

- `enqueue` persists a request and returns its native ULID. Throws INVALID_URL, or INVALID_PAYLOAD with `validationErrors`, or INVALID_PAYLOAD with no `validationErrors` when native rejects, most often because the queue is full.
- `enqueueBatch` is atomic. On invalid input it throws one INVALID_PAYLOAD with every issue in `validationErrors`, each with `itemIndex`.
- `removeItem` and `clearQueue` act on items in any status, FAILED rows included.
- `getQueueSize` and `getPendingItems` cover PENDING items only, cooling ones included. Items in flight and FAILED rows are excluded. `getPendingItems` returns dispatch order.

## Sync Functions

```typescript
function flush(): Promise<SyncResult>;
function drainUntilEmpty(options?: DrainOptions): Promise<DrainResult>;
function cancelDrain(): void;
function pauseSync(): Promise<void>;
function resumeSync(): Promise<void>;
function isSyncing(): Promise<boolean>;
```

- `flush` runs one cycle. The strategy plays no part. It does not check connectivity, so calling it offline can spend attempts. Per-item failures never reject: it rejects with NETWORK_ERROR only when the cycle itself dies. With nothing eligible it resolves 0/0 and emits SYNC_SUCCEEDED. While a cycle is running, iOS returns the last result and Android waits and runs its own.
- `drainUntilEmpty` flushes until `getQueueSize() === 0 && isSyncing() === false`. It sleeps until the soonest cooldown by itself, and stops at once with TIMEOUT if that is past the deadline. It does not flush while `getConnectionStatus()` is DISCONNECTED. `timeoutMs` and `cancelDrain()` are hard stops. A native cycle already running keeps going after the drain returns. Only one drain may run: a concurrent call throws DRAIN_ALREADY_ACTIVE, so await the previous drain, also after `cancelDrain()`.
- `pauseSync` persists. Workers and BGTasks stay inert while the app is dead. It lasts until `resumeSync()` or the next launch that reaches the library, including a JS reload. A launch clears it without emitting RESUMED.
- `resumeSync` dispatches pending items unless the strategy is MANUAL. If offline, the flush waits for connectivity.

## Configuration Functions

```typescript
function configureSync(options: SyncOptions): Promise<void>;
function getSyncConfig(): Promise<SyncOptions>;
```

`configureSync` replaces the whole configuration and persists it, so a worker or BGTask with no JS honors it. Android applies it from the next cycle, iOS from the next item. Omitting `defaultHeaders` deletes the stored copy: that is the logout path. Call it whenever the token changes: the library does not refresh tokens.

## History Functions

```typescript
function getLastSyncResult(): Promise<SyncResult | undefined>;
function getSyncHistory(limit?: number): Promise<SyncResult[]>;
function clearSyncHistory(): Promise<void>;
```

History is most recent first, includes 0/0 cycles, and is not trimmed automatically.

## Connection

```typescript
function getConnectionStatus(): Promise<ConnectionState>;
```

## Background Sync

```typescript
function enableBackgroundSync(options: BackgroundSyncOptions): Promise<void>;
function disableBackgroundSync(): Promise<void>;
function isBackgroundSyncEnabled(): Promise<boolean>;
```

- `enableBackgroundSync` schedules BGTaskScheduler or WorkManager work. Throws BACKGROUND_TASK_REGISTRATION_FAILED, for example on an iOS simulator or with `com.gabriel-sisjr.syncprovider.background` missing from Info.plist.
- The OS decides when a window runs. iOS does not launch a force-quit app for background work.
- Each window runs one cycle.
- `isBackgroundSyncEnabled` reports intent: it stays true with `foregroundOnly`.

## Events

```typescript
function addSyncEventListener(callback: (event: SyncEvent) => void): Promise<string>;
function removeSyncEventListener(subscriptionId: string): Promise<void>;
const SYNC_EVENT_CHANNEL = 'sync-event';
```

Events reach a running JS engine only.

## React Hooks

```typescript
function useConnection(): {
  status: ConnectionStatus;
  type: ConnectionType;
  isOnline: boolean;
  isMetered: boolean;
};

function useSyncQueue(): {
  size: number;
  items: SyncItem[];
  isLoading: boolean;
  error: SyncError | null; // failed refresh only: methods reject
  enqueue(input: SyncItemInput): Promise<string>;
  enqueueBatch(inputs: SyncItemInput[]): Promise<string[]>;
  removeItem(id: string): Promise<boolean>;
  clearQueue(): Promise<void>;
  refresh(): Promise<void>;
};

function useSyncStatus(): {
  isSyncing: boolean;
  isPaused: boolean;
  progress: number | null; // SYNC_PROGRESS is iOS-only
  lastResult: SyncResult | null;
  error: SyncError | null;
  flush(): Promise<SyncResult>;
  pause(): Promise<void>;
  resume(): Promise<void>;
};

function useOfflineQueue(): {
  connection: UseConnectionResult;
  size: number;
  items: SyncItem[];
  isSyncing: boolean;
  isWaitingForConnection: boolean;
  error: SyncError | null;
  enqueue(input: SyncItemInput): Promise<string>;
  flush(): Promise<SyncResult>;
};

function useSyncEvents(options: {
  onEvent: (event: SyncEvent) => void;
  types?: SyncEventType[];
  enabled?: boolean; // default true
}): void;

function useSyncConfig(): {
  config: SyncOptions | null;
  isLoading: boolean;
  error: SyncError | null;
  setConfig(next: SyncOptions): Promise<void>; // updates the calling hook only
  refresh(): Promise<void>;
};

function useAutoSync(options: {
  enabled?: boolean;              // default false: the hook is inert until true
  intervalMs?: number;            // default 60000; not positive falls back to it
  flushOnReconnect?: boolean;     // default true
  flushOnMetered?: boolean;       // default false; reconnect trigger only
  flushOnAppForeground?: boolean; // default false
  flushOnForeground?: boolean;    // reserved, ignored
  backgroundSync?: BackgroundSyncOptions; // reserved, ignored
}): void;

function useSyncSnapshot(): UseSyncSnapshotResult;

function useSyncContext(): {
  config: SyncOptions | undefined;
  hasProvider: boolean;
};
```

`useAutoSync`'s interval checks neither connectivity nor queue size: offline ticks can spend attempts. Gate `enabled` on `useConnection().isOnline` to stop ticking offline.

## Context

```tsx
<SyncProvider options={syncOptions} backgroundSync={backgroundOptions}>
  <App />
</SyncProvider>
```

Optional. It calls `configureSync(options)` on mount and on every change to `options`, reads the native config even if that rejects, and calls `enableBackgroundSync` when `backgroundSync` is passed, with a matching `disableBackgroundSync` on unmount. Keep `options` stable. Every hook works without it.

## Types

```typescript
interface SyncItemInput {
  method: HttpMethod;
  url: string;                       // absolute http(s)
  headers?: Record<string, string>;  // stored in plain text
  body?: string;                     // sent as UTF-8; stored in plain text
  contentType?: string;              // set here, not in headers
  priority?: SyncPriority;           // default NORMAL
  metadata?: Record<string, string>; // not sent, not echoed on events
}

interface SyncItem {
  id: string;           // native ULID; not sent with the request
  method: HttpMethod;
  url: string;
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
  body?: string;
  contentType?: string;
  priority?: SyncPriority;
  createdAt: number;
  attempts: number;     // 0 = never tried
  nextRetryAt: number;  // 0 = never attempted; eligible when <= now
  metadata?: Record<string, string>;
}

interface SyncOptions {
  strategy: SyncStrategy;
  retryPolicy: RetryPolicy;
  batchSize?: number;                      // default 25
  requestTimeoutMs?: number;               // default 30000
  maxQueueSize?: number;                   // default 10000; below 1 means 1
  persistQueue?: boolean;                  // stored, not used
  defaultHeaders?: Record<string, string>; // encrypted at rest
}

interface RetryPolicy {
  maxAttempts: number;          // the first attempt counts as one
  backoff: BackoffStrategy;
  baseDelayMs: number;
  maxDelayMs: number;
  jitter: boolean;              // factor in [0.75, 1.25)
  retryOnStatusCodes: number[]; // 401 and 403 stay permanent even if listed
}

interface SyncResult {
  startedAt: number;
  finishedAt: number;
  successCount: number;
  failureCount: number;           // permanent failures only
  succeededIds: string[];         // always empty on iOS
  failedIds: string[];            // always empty on iOS
  errors: Record<string, string>; // "<CODE>: <detail>"; always empty on iOS
}

interface DrainOptions {
  maxIterations?: number;        // default 32; counts real flushes
  timeoutMs?: number;            // default 60000; hard deadline
  delayBetweenCyclesMs?: number;
}

interface DrainResult {
  iterations: number;
  itemsDispatched: number;       // best effort; not a success count
  queueRemaining: number;
  stoppedReason: 'EMPTY' | 'MAX_ITERATIONS' | 'TIMEOUT' | 'CANCELLED';
}

interface BackgroundSyncOptions {
  minimumIntervalMs: number;          // Android floor 15 min; iOS soft hint
  requiresCharging?: boolean;         // iOS: processing task only
  requiresUnmeteredNetwork?: boolean; // Android only
  requiresDeviceIdle?: boolean;       // Android only
  foregroundOnly?: boolean;           // schedule no OS background work
  taskIdentifier?: string;            // stored, not used
}

interface ConnectionState {
  status: ConnectionStatus;
  type: ConnectionType;
  isInternetReachable?: boolean;
  isExpensive?: boolean;
}

interface SyncEvent {
  type: SyncEventType;
  timestamp: number;
  itemId?: string;
  progress?: number;
  errorCode?: SyncErrorCode;
  statusCode?: number;
  attempt?: number;
  connectionStatus?: ConnectionStatus;
  metadata?: Record<string, string>; // iOS diagnostics, not the item's metadata
}

class SyncError extends Error {
  readonly code: SyncErrorCode;
  readonly cause?: unknown;
  readonly validationErrors?: ValidationIssue[];
}

type ValidationIssue = {
  field: string;
  reason: string;
  value?: unknown; // only for method, priority and contentType
  itemIndex?: number;
};
```

## Enums

### SyncStrategy
- `AUTOMATIC` — The engine retries on its own, and dispatches pending items on `resumeSync()`.
- `MANUAL` — The engine schedules nothing on its own: no retry timer, no Android retry kick. Background windows still run if you called `enableBackgroundSync`.
- `OPPORTUNISTIC` — Reserved. Behaves like `AUTOMATIC`.

### SyncPriority
`HIGH`, `NORMAL`, `LOW`.

### BackoffStrategy
- `LINEAR` — `delay = baseDelayMs * attempt`.
- `EXPONENTIAL` — `delay = baseDelayMs * 2^(attempt-1)`.
- `FIBONACCI` — `delay = baseDelayMs * fib(attempt)`.

All capped at `maxDelayMs`.

### SyncEventType
- `ITEM_ENQUEUED`, `ITEM_REMOVED` (from `removeItem` only).
- `SYNC_STARTED`, `SYNC_PROGRESS` (iOS only).
- `SYNC_SUCCEEDED` — No permanent failure, including 0/0 cycles.
- `SYNC_FAILED` — A permanent failure, or the cycle died. `errorCode` is set only when it died.
- `ITEM_SUCCEEDED`, `ITEM_FAILED`, `ITEM_RETRYING`.
- `QUEUE_CLEARED`, `CONNECTION_CHANGED`, `PAUSED`, `RESUMED`.
- `BACKGROUND_SYNC_STARTED`, `BACKGROUND_SYNC_COMPLETED`.

### ConnectionStatus
`CONNECTED`, `DISCONNECTED`, `METERED`, `UNKNOWN`.

### ConnectionType
`WIFI`, `CELLULAR`, `ETHERNET`, `BLUETOOTH`, `VPN`, `OTHER`, `NONE`, `UNKNOWN`.

### SyncErrorCode
- `NETWORK_ERROR` — Transport failure, on item events. Also what `flush` rejects with when its cycle dies.
- `SERVER_ERROR` — A response outside 2xx, other than 401/403, on item events.
- `TIMEOUT` — `requestTimeoutMs` exceeded, on item events.
- `UNAUTHORIZED` — 401 or 403, on item events.
- `MAX_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED` — A retriable failure with no attempts left, on ITEM_FAILED.
- `INVALID_PAYLOAD` — Validation failure with `validationErrors`, or a native rejection without them in most functions.
- `INVALID_URL` — From `enqueue`. `enqueueBatch` reports it under INVALID_PAYLOAD.
- `QUEUE_FULL` — Raised by native, but reaches JS as INVALID_PAYLOAD for now.
- `DUPLICATE_ITEM` — Reserved. Neither platform raises it.
- `BACKGROUND_TASK_REGISTRATION_FAILED` — From the background functions.
- `NATIVE_MODULE_UNAVAILABLE` — Web, SSR, or the native module is not linked.
- `DRAIN_ALREADY_ACTIVE` — A drain is already running or settling.

## Credentials in a process with no JS

- `defaultHeaders` are encrypted at rest: Android Keystore AES-256-GCM, iOS Keychain (`AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`).
- On a 401 or 403 in a process that has not called `configureSync`, the item stays PENDING, no attempt is spent, the next try waits at least 60 seconds, and the cycle stops.
- If stored headers cannot be read, nothing is dispatched and items wait. `configureSync` ends the wait. While they are unreadable, `getSyncConfig()` returns none, so re-applying it deletes them.

## Platform Support

| Feature               | iOS                                      | Android                                        |
|-----------------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Persistence           | Core Data                                | Room                                           |
| Background sync       | BGTaskScheduler (refresh + processing)   | WorkManager (periodic + opt-in retry kick)     |
| Dispatcher            | URLSession (foreground + background)     | OkHttp + Coroutines                            |
| Batch dispatch        | One item at a time                       | Concurrent                                     |
| Connectivity          | NWPathMonitor                            | ConnectivityManager + NetworkCallback          |
| Recovery              | RecoveryManager, on every engine start   | RecoveryWorker, on JS attach, boot, app update |
| Persisted config      | UserDefaults + Keychain                  | SharedPreferences + Android Keystore           |
| Privacy Manifest      | Shipped (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy)          | n/a                                            |
| Min OS                | iOS 15                                   | Android 7.0 (API 24)                           |
